support.title: Diagnose fast, fix properly
support.intro: During my internship at Cekoya, I took part in client support: network incidents, unavailable services, unstable workstations, printing, access to resources. Support is mostly a method: identify, isolate, fix, then confirm.
support.mission: Network incident: shares and printers unreachable on several workstations after a router or switch change. Goal: restore access quickly without disrupting production further.
support.context: Several users report unreachable shared folders, missing printers and unstable connections. The issue seems limited to one part of the network.
support.objective: Restore access to shares, printers and apps, check stability, then confirm with the affected users.
support.role: DHCP/DNS, a VLAN mistake, a faulty cable or port, an address conflict: the first step was to find out whether the workstations or the network were at fault.
actions: Check whether one workstation or several are affected
Check addressing: IP, gateway, DNS, DHCP lease
Test access: ping the gateway, the server, shares and printers
Isolate the area: switch port, VLAN, equipment linked to the affected workstations
Fix, then confirm with a real case (a share and a print job)
support.proofText: Support takes technical skills, but above all a clear method to cut downtime while leaving a clean result.

impacts.title: Prioritize
impacts.text: I fix what blocks the most first (access to essential resources), then check stability before closing.

impacts.title: Confirm
impacts.text: A fix is never assumed: I test it on a real workstation, then check with users that everything is back to normal.

project.title: Deploying a 4G backup connection
project.intro: Assignment carried out during my internship at Cekoya, in a managed-services context with business clients (small companies, shops, public bodies).
project.mission: I handled the technical side of the 4G router: preparation, configuration, failover and testing. The goal: deliver a reliable setup, ready to install at the client's site.
project.context: A client kept losing its main internet connection, which blocked its business tools, IP phones and day-to-day work.
project.objective: Switch automatically to a backup connection, with no manual action, to limit the impact of outages.
project.role: Preparation, configuration, failover and testing on my own; on-site integration with a senior technician.
actions: Prepare the 4G link: SIM card, carrier settings, secured admin access
Configure automatic failover between the main line and 4G
Detect the outage and fail back once the main line is stable
Simulate outages to check the switch to 4G and its stability
Confirm the automatic return to the main line
project.proofText: The setup passes when the client keeps a working connection during an outage, and both failover and failback happen on their own, reliably.

impacts.title: Reliability
impacts.text: Simple to maintain, failover tested in realistic conditions before going live.

impacts.title: Working in a pair
impacts.text: Technical preparation on my own, on-site integration and final validation with the senior technician.

assistance.title: Fix it, then help the user help themselves
assistance.intro: During my internship at Cekoya, I was often in direct contact with users, remotely or on-site. The goal: solve the incident quickly while explaining what's going on and what I'm doing.
assistance.mission: Deploying a new workstation after an incident, with the user's environment restored and network checks.
assistance.context: A user could no longer work: slowdowns, crashes, random access to network drives, printing and apps. The priority was to get them working again fast.
assistance.objective: Provide a stable workstation, restore accounts, access and tools, and show the user simple checks they can do alone.
assistance.role: Workstation install and setup, domain rejoin if needed, DHCP/DNS, share and printer checks, then follow-up with the user.
actions: Prepare a clean workstation: updates, drivers, base settings
Check access: shares, printing, apps, browsing
Explain what was done and how to avoid it happening again
Have the user test their real tasks before closing
assistance.proofText: Assistance isn't just repairing: it means turning a technical problem into simple steps for the user.

impacts.title: Explain simply
impacts.text: I describe what I do without jargon and leave two or three quick checks the user can redo alone (Wi-Fi, cable, restart).

impacts.title: Close on real use
impacts.text: The user tests their usual tasks. The ticket is only closed when the workstation actually works.

inventory.title: Track the assets, avoid surprises
inventory.intro: Asset management is the base of a clean IT system: knowing what hardware exists, where it is, what state it's in and who uses it. It's also what lets you anticipate failures and renewals.
inventory.mission: Updating a client's asset inventory: checking hardware on-site, consolidating the data and updating the records to make maintenance and support easier.
inventory.context: The client's inventory was incomplete: unlisted workstations, hardware that had changed hands, outdated details (model, serial number, location).
inventory.objective: A reliable inventory of workstations, peripherals and network gear, with enough traceability to speed up support and plan renewals.
inventory.role: On-site checks, data consolidation and inventory update. I also standardized some fields (names, locations, owners) so it stays readable over time.
actions: Check workstations, screens, printers and visible network gear on-site
Update model, serial number, condition, location and user
Apply a naming rule (PC-XXX, ROOM-XXX) to find things fast
Spot ghost hardware: listed in the tool but missing on-site, and the other way round
Gather what support needs: OS, static IP, warranty, machine role
inventory.proofText: The point isn't “doing an inventory”, it's structuring data reliable enough to be used every day for support, maintenance and security.

impacts.title: Field, tool, check
impacts.text: I collect, structure, then check that the information is consistent and reusable.

impacts.title: Fewer incidents
impacts.text: A clean inventory speeds up troubleshooting (which hardware, where, for whom) and helps track updates.

communication.title: Communicate to convince
communication.intro: How Cekoya communicates externally (image, acquisition, credibility), and how I apply the same logic to my own projects: content and services.
communication.mission: Cekoya relies on several complementary channels: a showcase website, LinkedIn, Google presence and reviews, partnerships and trade shows. The goal: be visible, earn trust and create opportunities.
communication.context: Website (first impression), LinkedIn (professional image and network), Google (being found and recommended), partnerships (credibility on the ground), trade shows (visibility and trust).
communication.objective: Communication that holds up: the same message everywhere, backed by reputation.
communication.role: Analysing the communication channels, then applying the same logic to my projects: show, reassure, convert. My content is the proof.
actions: Content: attract with proof by showing the level (pacing, transitions, sound design)
Trust: clear expectations, stated deadlines, precise feedback
Offer: what's included, how it works, what gets delivered
Website: reassure from the first impression
LinkedIn: build credibility and make contacts
communication.proofText: I know how to sell with proof: content that reassures, a clear pitch and a simple offer. It's the same base as effective external communication in a company.

impacts.title: One consistent message
impacts.text: The same pitch on the website, LinkedIn and Google; partners and client feedback back it up.

watch.title: Tech watch
watch.topic: How server virtualization evolved, from VMware to today

before.title: Before virtualization
before.text: One physical server, one service. The result: machines running at 10-20% of capacity, high costs, little flexibility and critical failures.

vmware.title: VMware arrives
vmware.text: In the late 1990s, the hypervisor separates hardware from the operating system: one physical machine hosts several isolated servers.

today.title: VMware today
today.text: ESXi, vSphere and vCenter are still enterprise standards.
features: vMotion: move a VM with no downtime
Snapshots: roll back to a previous state quickly
vSAN: distributed storage without a physical SAN
HA: automatic VM restart after a failure

broadcom.title: Since the Broadcom acquisition
broadcom.text: Broadcom closed its acquisition of VMware in November 2023, then replaced perpetual licenses with bundled subscriptions and dropped the free ESXi in early 2024. Many companies and homelabs started looking at Proxmox VE and Hyper-V, which is also why I practice all three.

watch.sources: Sources: Google Alerts, LeMondeInformatique, ZDNet, Tom's Hardware, VMware Community, Reddit r/sysadmin

overview.title: Lab
overview.text: My training ground since 2022: a pfSense firewall, Cisco and MikroTik switches, an ESXi host and Zabbix watching over all of it, plus a Hyper-V lab for school. Whatever I learn in class or at work, I rebuild here before I call it learned.

map.title: Network map
map.hint: Hover or select a node to see its role and what it connects to.

internet.label: Internet
internet.role: Internet uplink. The ISP box runs in bridge mode: pfSense holds the public address, and only the WireGuard port is open.

vps01.role: Ubuntu VPS hosting this site behind Nginx and Let's Encrypt. It joins the homelab through a site-to-site WireGuard tunnel: metrics to Zabbix, backups to the NAS, access to the staging site in the DMZ.

fw01.role: Firewall and router between VLANs: every flow from one to another goes through an explicit rule. It also runs the WireGuard admin VPN and the Unbound DNS resolver.

sw-core.role: MikroTik core switch: 802.1Q trunks to pfSense and the hosts, per-VLAN access ports for everything else.

sw-lab.role: Cisco practice switch: I use it to work on the IOS CLI and to connect the PC running the Hyper-V lab.

ap01.role: Wi-Fi access point: one network for personal devices (VLAN 50) and an isolated one for guests and IoT (VLAN 60).

esxi01.role: Main hypervisor: a second-hand tower, picked for being quiet and having ECC RAM. One port group per VLAN on the vSwitch.

nas01.role: RAID 1 NAS: target for the Veeam and VPS backups, with an encrypted off-site copy every week.

dc01.role: Test domain controller (lab.yexo.lan): I rebuild GPOs and AD structures here before using them anywhere else.

zbx01.role: Zabbix: SNMP for pfSense, switches and the NAS, VMware template for ESXi, agent 2 on the VMs and on the VPS through the tunnel. Alerts go to Discord.

bkp01.role: Nightly VM backups to the NAS, with 14 restore points. One test restore a month: a backup you never restored isn't a backup.

rp01.role: Nginx reverse proxy in the DMZ. It only receives traffic coming from the VPS through the tunnel and can't open anything towards the LAN.

hv-lab.role: PC running the Hyper-V school lab: a Debian server (DHCP, FTP, MariaDB, inter-VLAN routing), a Windows Server, a Windows client and a Linux client, on an isolated vSwitch.

clients.label: clients
clients.role: PCs, phones, console and IoT devices. IoT and guests only get internet access.

items.admin: Management interfaces: pfSense, ESXi, switches, access point and NAS. Reachable only through the WireGuard VPN.
items.srv: Internal servers: test AD, Zabbix, GLPI, Veeam and Docker. The home network only reaches the ports it needs (DNS, web).
items.dmz: What's exposed: reverse proxy and the site's staging copy. Reachable only through the VPS tunnel, with no way into the LAN.
items.lab: The Hyper-V school lab, isolated from everything else with internet access only. I can break anything there safely.
items.home: Personal network: PCs, phones and console. Internet and internal DNS.
items.iot: Guests and IoT devices: internet only, with client isolation.

resources.title: Resources
resources.text: Each use gets its own VLAN, and pfSense filters everything that crosses from one to another. On the ISP box, only the WireGuard port is open: anything public goes through the VPS, then through the tunnel to the reverse proxy in the DMZ. VMs are backed up every night to the NAS, with an off-site copy every week. Zabbix watches the hardware, the VMs and the VPS, and warns me before anyone else notices an outage.

converter.title: Sensitivity converter
converter.intro: Switch games without relearning your aim: the converter keeps the same mouse distance for a full turn (cm/360).

how.title: How it works
how.text: Each game multiplies your sensitivity by a coefficient, the yaw. The converter works out how far your mouse travels for a full turn, then the sensitivity that gives the same distance in the target game.
how.note: Result rounded to 4 decimals. The dot is the decimal separator, as in games.
